title: Cost Per Kilometer Calculator
description: Turn any journey's total cost into a per-kilometre figure with the Cost Per Kilometer Calculator — for comparing trips and vehicles. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a €96 trip over 412 km works out to €0.23 per kilometre — the figure that finally makes the train ticket comparable.
quick_answer: The Cost Per Kilometer Calculator divides a journey's total cost by its distance in kilometres and returns the per-kilometre figure that makes trips comparable. Enter what the journey cost and how far it went, and read the unit price of your travel in whatever currency you spent.

faq: What costs can I include?
Whatever the journey truly cost you: fuel, tolls, parking, wear allowances, a hire charge. Consistency across comparisons matters more than any particular list.
Does it include currency conversion?
No — the calculator divides in the currency you enter. Convert the total first if the trip crossed currencies.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Cost per kilometre is accounting, not routing; traffic affects time, and only affects cost through the categories you enter.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Because roads are not straight lines. Use the road distance — it is what the journey actually cost you to cover.
Can route results change over time?
Road distances barely change; costs do. Recalculate per trip rather than trusting last year's figure.
Cost per km or per mile?
Whichever your odometer and audience use. The two pages are twins; 1 mile = 1.609344 km converts between their answers.
Is a lower figure always better?
It is cheaper, not better: comfort, time and reliability are also purchased in a journey's total. The unit cost informs the choice; it does not make it.
Return trip — double the distance, same figure?
Yes if costs scale with distance; fixed additions (a day's parking) dilute over the doubled distance and the per-km figure falls. Both effects are real; the calculator shows them.
My car reports mpg — wrong page?
Convert your totals once (miles × 1.609344 = km) or use the Cost Per Mile Calculator, which speaks mpg-era units natively.
Is cost per km used for reimbursement?
Many employers and tax systems publish per-km allowances; this tool computes your actual figure to compare against them, not the allowance itself.
